full_source_claim_and_standing_assumptio: One fixed input-free randomized machine is used at every sample size. It reads a ternary random tape to a delimiter, parses a binary prefix as a machine/input, simulates it, and tags a halting output, with fallback 0. Proposition A.1 asserts undecidable membership in its support by encoding arbitrary halting instances. No language family, learner distribution or rate premise. Full-support tape law and unambiguous coding are implicit. The printed branch tests r=1 after defining b; divergence on encoded nonhalting machines is possible. These source issues are retained, not silently repaired.

full_source_claim_and_standing_assumptio: For each indexed countable family L with ordinary membership access and correct full-language subset oracle S, choose one generating algorithm G before the target K and positive enumeration. On every target enumeration that G eventually has nonempty support within K minus observed strings. If the same L is identifiable, the same G eventually has support exactly K minus observed strings. G receives no tell-tale input. Infinite targets are the usual generation convention; finite exhaustion is separately qualified in Definition 12. This is an adversarial-enumeration limit claim, without statistical rates.
strength: Exact full fresh support for an arbitrary predicted index is faithful on all-infinite OracleFamily. Online breadth is proved after assuming an already stably identifying A, a stronger input premise than the source combined subset-oracle guarantee. Universal consistency for non-identifiable families and the combined same-witness corollary were not found; no total strength ordering applies to the full claims.
algorithm_scope: Named sampler maps a geometric seed through oracle search for a fresh point in the selected language. Native subset selection and sampler are represented separately. A candidate composition is evident but its full best-of-both-worlds correctness is not newly certified. Selected semantic support signatures do not by themselves certify ordinary computation or an effective support query.

full_source_claim_and_standing_assumptio: For each identifiable indexed countable family L, correct membership access and subset oracle S, there is one algorithm A for every target K and every positive enumeration which eventually stabilizes to a fixed index denoting K, without receiving any tell-tale. The raw last-critical selection eventually denotes K and can vary among duplicate indices; the source explicitly adds lowest-index finite-projection post-processing (Lemma 5.4). Each round restricts to consistent indices up to its time and selects the greatest critical index. No rate or computable cutoff is stated.
strength: Raw last-critical algorithm is equivalent modulo indexing/default. FiniteWitnessIdentifies strengthens raw extensional eventual correctness to all long consistent lists containing a finite witness, under mere finite-tell-tale existence. It does not assert fixed-index stabilization, so the full source identification theorem is only partial; stronger extensional scope and weaker index conclusion oppose one another.
algorithm_scope: One fixed nonadaptive finite truth-table program queries membership and whole-language inclusion and selects the last critical index below input-list length, default 0. It takes no tell-tale argument. Ordinary computability requires Computable2 of both query functions; arbitrary oracle correctness alone is not ordinary computability. Source projection-based stabilization is not the native finite-table postprocessor.
discrepancies: FiniteWitnessIdentifies concludes C(A xs)=Ci, not A(prefix_t)=one fixed name.
No native composition implementing the source Lemma 5.4 stabilization for this subset learner was found.
Source empty-version-space fallback outputs an element of X where an index is required; native default 0 is well typed.
